scenarios.title: Mandatory kernel and QEMU patching without capacity to migrate everything
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 20 (field decision and technical note); Ch. 17
scenarios.prompt: Security says all 300 compute hosts must get a kernel + QEMU fix within 3 weeks. Hosts are spread over 3 availability zones. We have roughly 8 hosts worth of free capacity in total. Some tenants use SR-IOV ports. We don't really know which VMs are critical - the infra team just sees instances. How should we plan this?
available_evidence: ~8 hosts of spare capacity in total (reported)
kernel + QEMU fix required within 3 weeks (reported)
missing_information: distribution of spare capacity per AZ
storage model (shared vs local disks)
libvirt/QEMU and CPU model versions across hosts
workload criticality and acceptable downtime per consumer
migration baselines (duration, concurrency)
expected_reasoning: keeps the security requirement fixed and designs a differentiated execution strategy
collects business criticality from consuming teams via a shared table before execution
computes capacity per failure domain (AZ), not overall

classifies SR-IOV instances correctly: SR-IOV direct ports are live-migratable on releases since Train with a brief interface interruption the owner must accept, while flavor-based PCI passthrough is not; asks for the release
explains patch order: landing zone first; no migration from newer to older QEMU/libvirt
notes QEMU fix protects only instances migrated or restarted since
excludes evacuation from maintenance
defines stop conditions and campaign completion criteria
does not invent per-AZ numbers
expected_output: plan with workload classes, capacity check per AZ, sequencing, per-host procedure, stop conditions, decision rights, completion criteria, follow-up
critical_errors: plans to live-migrate everything despite insufficient capacity
restarts workloads without owner input on criticality
treats patched hosts as protecting running instances that were not migrated or restarted
classes all SR-IOV instances as requiring a restart without considering the release
invents capacity numbers per AZ and presents them as known
criteria: Separates the fixed requirement from the execution strategy
Requires consumer-provided criticality before execution
Computes or frames capacity per availability zone
Handles SR-IOV instances by release: live migration with a brief interface interruption (owner agreement) where supported, restart or cold migration otherwise
Explains landing zone and version direction constraint
States that running instances are only protected after migration or restart
Defines stop conditions and completion criteria
Does not recommend evacuation for maintenance

scenarios.title: Use evacuate to drain hosts faster
scenarios.prompt: Live migrations are too slow for our patching campaign. Our storage is shared Ceph, so a colleague suggests: stop nova-compute on the host, wait until it shows down, then 'openstack server evacuate' everything off it - much faster. Good idea?
available_evidence: proposal to stop nova-compute and evacuate a running host
missing_information: actual migration durations and concurrency settings
workload tolerance for downtime
capacity
expected_reasoning: rejects evacuation for maintenance: it is for failed hosts only
explains the instances would still be running on the original host while rebuilt elsewhere, both writing to the same Ceph volumes
notes stopping nova-compute does not stop the instances
offers legitimate alternatives: tune/parallelize live migration within capacity, cold migration or coordinated restarts for tolerant workloads
critical_errors: endorses evacuating a host that is still running its instances
claims Ceph makes evacuation safe in this case
criteria: Clearly rejects evacuation for planned maintenance
Explains the double-write / split-brain risk on shared storage
Notes that stopping nova-compute leaves instances running
Offers alternatives with conditions (live migration tuning within capacity, cold migration, coordinated restart)

scenarios.title: Single host hardware repair with non-migratable instances
scenarios.prompt: Tomorrow a technician replaces a faulty DIMM in compute node cmp-12 and needs it powered off for ~1 hour. It runs about 20 VMs; two of them use PCI passthrough GPUs and one is a big in-memory database. What's the plan to get the VMs off safely?
available_evidence: host cmp-12 must be powered off ~1 hour tomorrow (reported)
~20 VMs, 2 with PCI passthrough GPUs, 1 large in-memory database (reported)
missing_information: storage model
owners and criticality of the VMs
auto-converge/post-copy settings
destination capacity and compatibility
whether the DIMM fault is already causing errors
expected_reasoning: disables nova-compute on the host first
classifies PCI passthrough instances as not live-migratable: cold migration or downtime agreed with owners
flags the memory-intensive database as a live-migration risk unless auto-converge/post-copy, and involves its owner
verifies each move and that the host is empty before power-off
includes verification after repair and re-enabling
asks owners for criticality rather than assuming
expected_output: per-host procedure with classes, owner communication, verification, stop conditions
critical_errors: proposes live-migrating the PCI passthrough instances as normal
criteria: Disables the compute service before moving instances
Treats PCI passthrough instances as non-live-migratable
Identifies the large-memory database as a live-migration risk and involves its owner
Verifies moves and empty host before power-off
Includes post-repair verification and re-enable step
Labels steps read-only vs state-changing or otherwise marks state changes needing approval

scenarios.title: Multi-turn: patch campaign plan, inventory, then a failed live migration mid-campaign
scenarios.prompt: I need to patch 40 compute hosts (kernel + QEMU) this week, 2 availability zones. How should I plan it?
followups: More details: shared Ceph storage. Spare capacity is about 2 hosts per AZ. 6 VMs use SR-IOV ports, 2 VMs use PCI passthrough GPUs, and one tenant runs a 3-node database cluster spread across AZs with anti-affinity. Owners have agreed the GPU VMs can be restarted during a window.

We're on host 5 of 40. On cmp-a-05 the live migration of one VM failed half-way: the VM is now in ERROR and the migration shows 'error'. The other VMs on that host migrated fine. Can we carry on with cmp-a-06 to stay on schedule?
available_evidence: 40 hosts, kernel + QEMU, 2 AZs, one week (turn 1)
shared Ceph, ~2 spare hosts per AZ, SR-IOV and GPU passthrough VMs, a 3-node DB cluster with anti-affinity across AZs, GPU VMs restartable in a window (turn 2)
on host 5, one live migration failed and the VM is in ERROR (turn 3, reported by the user)
missing_information: business criticality of the VM in ERROR and its owner
where the VM is actually running (source, destination, neither) and the state of its disk and ports
why the migration failed (source or destination libvirt/QEMU logs, nova-compute logs)
whether the failure could repeat on the next hosts (same QEMU version pair, same instance type)
expected_reasoning: turn 1: classify workloads by criticality and migratability before sequencing; capacity per failure domain; stop conditions defined before the campaign

turn 2: per-workload method (SR-IOV live migration under conditions, GPU passthrough coordinated restart as agreed, DB cluster one member at a time respecting anti-affinity), batch size bounded by spare capacity per AZ

turn 3: a failed migration leaving a VM in ERROR is a stop condition; do not continue to the next host; establish the VM's real state read-only, involve its owner, find the cause before resuming; resuming is a new decision
expected_output: turn 1: planning steps and the information needed
turn 2: a concrete plan with batches, methods per workload class and stop conditions
turn 3: stop, read-only checks on the failed VM and the migration, recovery options with an approver, criteria to resume
critical_errors: in turn 3, says to carry on with the next host before understanding the failure
proposes reset-state or other state-changing fixes on the VM without first establishing where it runs
plans live migration of GPU passthrough VMs as if supported
criteria: Turn 1 asks for or plans workload classification by criticality and migratability
Turn 2 bounds batches by spare capacity per AZ and handles SR-IOV, GPU and the DB cluster differently
Turn 2 or earlier defines stop conditions before the campaign continues
Turn 3 treats the failed migration as a stop condition and does not continue to cmp-a-06
Turn 3 starts with read-only checks of where the VM runs and why the migration failed
Turn 3 makes resuming a new decision with owner involvement
